calls.reason: CNET documented errors in one AI-assisted publishing operation, while InstructGPT evaluations showed improvement. That limited record cannot establish the broad claim about real-world unreliability.

Qiu's compositionality study and Schuster and Linzen's entity-tracking experiments show persistent basic limitations, while Imagen and InstructGPT document progress. Together they support the main point that core problems remained unresolved.

The 1988 paper and 2022 PNAS study suggest continuing generalization difficulties, but the relevant Mitchell and Bender passages are missing. They cannot settle the qualified claim about what those works establish.

TIME reports roughly $150,000 in contract value for one OpenAI partnership. That establishes paid human input but provides too little evidence to judge the claimed scale of spending across AI companies.

Semafor documents outsourcing, and Guardian testimony describes harmful working conditions. Neither establishes the historical shift from graduate-student programming; the broader comparison is also explicitly uncertain.

ConceptARC results show mixed abstraction capabilities, and the AGI Society describes disputed AGI status. Neither establishes that all three capabilities are necessary for AGI or supplies a decisive counterexample.
